desc: SEPRA is the name GEPAN carried from 1988 to 2004 and the name under which the French service appears in the COMETA report. The renaming is itself informative: the office was rebadged in 1988 as the Atmospheric Re-entry Phenomena Expertise Department, a title that describes space-debris re-entry rather than UAP, and only in 2000 was the acronym redefined to Service d'Expertise des Phénomènes Rares Aérospatiaux, rare aerospace phenomena. Jean-Jacques Velasco headed it throughout. The Gendarmerie routing arrangement continued, giving SEPRA access to a national database of reports, and CNES technical resources remained available for physical-trace cases such as Trans-en-Provence in 1981. COMETA's second recommendation was directed squarely at this office: boost SEPRA's human and material resources, extend its collection to all of Europe and worldwide, maintain and develop its databases, and raise its foreign-relations status. The service was renamed GEIPAN in 2005 and Velasco was succeeded by Jacques Patenet.
